pass_a_gloss: Therefore ivory he said, such as Paul says deacons grave, not to much wine attending. King bound in the runnings. Or also otherwise, bond of the peoples' love to be led he says into royal priesthood. Or also in your delight, in your love, because of some even of the righteous themselves being reckoned. To the clusters the breasts are likened, to those having the spiritual gladness. Or because I the confession bring, and upon me his turning; either in the second coming, or also from the people of the Jews. Is sanctified therefore the food of the bride, Christ feasting together. That is, prays the sojourn of the Savior into Judea the Church to come about, according to providence of the one giving Him to men, that He may suck the God-bearer.
pass_b_english: That is why he called it ivory: such deacons as Paul calls dignified, not given to much wine (1 Timothy 3:8).

'A king bound in the galleries' (Song of Songs 7:5). Or, taken another way, he says that the bond of the peoples' love is brought into a royal priesthood (1 Peter 2:9). Or else, 'in your delight' (Song of Songs 7:6) means in your love, because some are reckoned even among the righteous themselves.

The breasts are likened to clusters (Song of Songs 7:7), clusters that hold spiritual gladness. Or it means that I bring the confession, and 'His turning is toward me' (Song of Songs 7:10), either at the second coming, or also from the people of the Jews. So the bride's food is made holy, since Christ feasts with her.

That is, the Church prays that the Savior may come to dwell in Judea, by the providence of the One who gives Him to mankind, so that He may nurse at the breast of the Mother of God (Song of Songs 8:1).
source_text:
καθαρᾷ συνειδήσει, ὁμολογοῦντες αὐτοῦ τὰ μυστήρια. ∆ιόπερ ἐλεφάντινον εἴρηκεν,
ὁποίους ὁ Παῦλός φησιν διακόνους σεμνοὺς, μὴ οἴνῳ πολλῷ προσέχοντας. Βασιλεὺς
δεδεμένος ἐν παραδρομαῖς. Ἢ καὶ ἄλλως, σύνδεσμον τῆς τῶν λαῶν ἀγάπης ἄγεσθαί
φησιν εἰς βασίλειον ἱεράτευμα. Ἢ καὶ ἐν τρυφῇ σου, τῇ ἀγάπῃ σου, διὰ τό τινα καὶ
αὐτῶν τῶν δικαίων νομίζεσθαι. Τοῖς δὲ βότρυσιν οἱ μασθοὶ ἀπεικάζονται, τοῖς
ἔχουσι τὴν πνευματικὴν εὐφροσύνην. Ἢ ὅτι ἐγὼ τὴν ὁμολογίαν προσάγω, καὶ ἐπ'
ἐμὲ ἡ ἐπιστροφὴ αὐτοῦ· ἢ ἐν τῇ παρουσίᾳ τῇ δευτέρᾳ, ἢ καὶ ἀπὸ τοῦ λαοῦ τῶν
Ἰουδαίων. Ἁγιάζεται τοίνυν ἡ τροφὴ τῆς νύμφης, συνευωχουμένου Χριστοῦ. Ἤγουν
εὔχεται τὴν ἐπιδημίαν τοῦ Σωτῆρος εἰς τὴν Ἰουδαίαν ἡ Ἐκκλησία γενέσθαι, κατὰ
πρόνοιαν τοῦ διδόντος αὐτὸν τοῖς ἀνθρώποις, ἵνα θηλάσῃ τὴν Θεοτόκον. Εὑροῦσά

notes: Source checked clause by clause against PG 69 col. 1292.
The row opens with the end of the sentence translated in u03-rem-early and closes with 'Εὑροῦσά', the first word of the lemma translated in u03-rem-close.
'διὰ τό τινα καὶ αὐτῶν τῶν δικαίων νομίζεσθαι' is obscure in the condensed fragment and is rendered literally.
'So the bride's food is made holy' has no surviving lemma; no reference is added.

The source row opens with 'καθαρᾷ συνειδήσει, ὁμολογοῦντες αὐτοῦ τὰ μυστήρια', the end of a sentence translated whole in u03-rem-early. It closes with 'Εὑροῦσά', the first word of the lemma 'Εὑροῦσά σε' (Song of Songs 8:1), which is translated in u03-rem-close.

'Βασιλεὺς δεδεμένος ἐν παραδρομαῖς' follows the LXX of Song of Songs 7:6 (English 7:5); παραδρομαί, literally 'runnings' or 'galleries', is rendered 'galleries'. The comment that explains the first reading has dropped out of the catena; only the alternative ('Or, taken another way') survives.
'διὰ τό τινα καὶ αὐτῶν τῶν δικαίων νομίζεσθαι' is obscure in this condensed fragment; rendered literally, 'because some are reckoned even among the righteous themselves'.
'τοῖς ἔχουσι' agrees with τοῖς βότρυσιν, so the clusters are what hold spiritual gladness.
'Ἢ ὅτι ἐγὼ τὴν ὁμολογίαν προσάγω, καὶ ἐπ' ἐμὲ ἡ ἐπιστροφὴ αὐτοῦ' glosses Song of Songs 7:11 LXX (English 7:10), 'I am my beloved's, and his turning is toward me'.
'So the bride's food is made holy' has no surviving lemma; it may refer to the stored fruits of Song of Songs 7:13, but no reference is added in the text.

'τοῦ διδόντος αὐτόν' answers the LXX of Song of Songs 8:1, 'Who would give you (τίς δῴη σε) as my brother, nursing at my mother's breasts'. 'The One who gives Him' means God, so it is capitalized. 'θηλάσῃ τὴν Θεοτόκον' (literally 'that He may suck the God-bearer') is rendered 'nurse at the breast of the Mother of God'.
Song verses use English numbering (LXX 7:6, 7:7, 7:8, 7:11 = English 7:5, 7:6, 7:7, 7:10).
